lessons.title: Principles of Organic Certification
lessons.body:
Organic certification means growing onions without synthetic chemicals and following strict rules. In Africa, many farmers sell to local markets without certification, but if you want to export or sell to supermarkets, certification helps. To get certified, you must follow organic standards for at least 3 years. This means no synthetic pesticides, herbicides, or fertilizers. You also cannot use genetically modified seeds. You must keep detailed records of everything you do: what you plant, when you plant, what you apply, and when you harvest. Records help inspectors see your practices.

Start by contacting a local certification body. In East Africa, the Kenya Organic Agriculture Network (KOAN) or similar groups can guide you. In West Africa, look for the African Organic Network (AfrONet). Certification costs moneyâbetween $200 and $1,000 per year, depending on the country. Smallholder groups can get group certification to share costs. You will need a buffer zone of at least 10 meters between your organic onions and non-organic fields to prevent chemical drift.

Your soil must be free of prohibited substances for 3 years. If you have used chemicals before, you must wait. During this transition, you can still sell onions as "transitional organic" in some markets. Use only allowed inputs: compost, manure, rock phosphate, and botanical pesticides like neem. Keep a diary of all activities. An inspector will visit your farm once a year. They will check your records, soil, and storage. If you pass, you get a certificate valid for one year.

Organic certification opens doors to premium pricesâoften 20-50% higher than conventional onions. But it requires commitment. Start small, keep good records, and join a farmer group for support. Even without certification, following organic principles improves soil health and reduces costs.

lessons.title: Organic Pest and Disease Management
lessons.body:
Onions face pests like thrips, onion maggots, and nematodes, and diseases like downy mildew and purple blotch. Organic management focuses on prevention first. Start with healthy soil: add compost to boost beneficial microbes. Rotate cropsânever plant onions in the same spot for at least 3 years. Plant resistant varieties like 'Red Creole' or 'Bombay Red'. Space plants 10-15 cm apart to allow airflow. Water in the morning so leaves dry before evening, reducing fungal diseases.

For thrips, use blue sticky trapsâ10 traps per acre. Spray neem oil (3 ml per liter of water) every 7 days if you see 5-10 thrips per plant. Add a few drops of soap to help it stick. For onion maggots, use row covers or plant radishes as a trap crop. Nematodes can be reduced by planting marigolds before onions. For downy mildew, spray a mixture of baking soda (1 tablespoon per liter) and soap every 10 days. Remove and burn infected leaves immediately.

Botanical pesticides are key. Tithonia (Mexican sunflower) leaves soaked in water for 24 hours make a strong spray against caterpillars. Garlic and chili pepper spray repels many insects. Always test on a few plants first. Encourage natural enemies: ladybugs eat aphids, and parasitic wasps attack caterpillars. Plant flowers like sunflowers and marigolds around your field to attract them.

Sanitation is critical. Clean tools with bleach solution (1 part bleach to 10 parts water) between uses. Remove crop debris after harvest. Store onions in cool, dry, well-ventilated place. If you must use a commercial organic pesticide, check with your certifier. Remember, organic doesn't mean no pesticidesâit means natural ones used responsibly. Monitor your field twice a week. Early detection saves your crop.

lessons.title: Cover Cropping and Green Manures
lessons.body:
Cover crops are plants grown to improve soil, not for harvest. They prevent erosion, add nutrients, and suppress weeds. For onions, use cover crops before planting or between seasons. Good choices in Africa include cowpeas, lablab, mucuna, and sunhemp. These legumes fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. A healthy cowpea crop can add 50-100 kg of nitrogen per hectare. That's like getting free fertilizer!

Plant cover crops during the rainy season when you're not growing onions. For example, after harvesting onions in June, plant cowpeas in July. They grow fast and cover the ground within 3-4 weeks. Before they flower, chop them down and leave them on the soil as mulch. This is called green manure. The mulch keeps moisture in, cools the soil, and feeds earthworms. You can also plant cover crops like rye or oats if you have them.

Another method is intercropping. Plant onions with a cover crop like clover or lettuce. But be carefulâonions don't like competition. Better to plant cover crops in separate beds or during fallow periods. If you have space, plant a border of sunhemp around your onion field. It attracts beneficial insects and acts as a windbreak.

To get the most from cover crops, inoculate legume seeds with rhizobia bacteria before planting. You can buy inoculant from agro-dealers. Sow seeds denselyâabout 50 kg per hectare for cowpeas. Water if dry. When plants are 30-40 cm tall, cut them at ground level and leave the roots in the soil. The roots decompose and improve soil structure. This reduces the need for compost. Over time, cover cropping increases organic matter, which helps onions grow bigger and healthier. It also reduces weeds by 50-70%.

lessons.title: Composting and Manure Management
lessons.body:
Compost is the backbone of organic onion farming. It provides nutrients, improves soil texture, and holds water. To make good compost, you need a mix of 'greens' (nitrogen-rich) and 'browns' (carbon-rich). Greens include fresh grass, kitchen scraps, and manure. Browns include dry leaves, straw, and cardboard. Aim for a ratio of 1 part greens to 3 parts browns by volume. A pile should be at least 1 cubic meter to heat up properly.

Build your compost in layers: 15 cm of browns, then 10 cm of greens, sprinkle a little soil or old compost, and repeat. Keep it as moist as a wrung-out sponge. Turn the pile every 2 weeks to add oxygen. It will heat up to 60Â°C, killing weed seeds and pathogens. After 6-8 weeks, it will be dark, crumbly, and smell earthy. Use it at 2-4 tonnes per hectare (about 2-4 kg per square meter) before planting onions.

Manure is also valuable but must be aged. Fresh manure can burn plants and carry diseases. Let it sit for at least 3 months. Poultry manure is rich in nitrogenâuse it sparingly (1-2 tonnes per hectare). Cow manure is milder. Never use human waste or pig manure on onions because of disease risk. Store manure under cover to prevent nutrients from washing away.

You can also make compost tea. Put 1 kg of compost in a cloth bag and soak in 10 liters of water for 3 days. Stir daily. Dilute 1:10 with water and spray on leaves or soil. This adds beneficial microbes. For onions, apply compost before planting and as a side-dress when bulbs start forming. Combine compost with wood ash (1 cup per square meter) for potassium. Good composting reduces your need for bought inputs and builds long-term soil fertility.

lessons.title: Conservation Tillage Practices
lessons.body:
Conservation tillage means disturbing the soil as little as possible. Instead of plowing deeply, you plant directly into the previous crop's residue. This saves labor, fuel, and protects soil life. For onions, which have shallow roots, conservation tillage helps keep soil structure intact. You can use a hand hoe to make small planting holes, or a jab planter. No need to turn the whole field.

Start by killing weeds without chemicals. You can slash them and leave them as mulch, or use a hoe to scrape the surface. If you have a lot of weeds, plant a cover crop like mucuna the season before. It will smother weeds. Then, when you're ready to plant onions, make a narrow furrow 2-3 cm deep and drop seeds or transplants. The mulch from previous crops keeps moisture in and prevents new weeds.

Conservation tillage increases earthworm populations. Earthworms tunnel through soil, improving drainage and mixing organic matter. After 2-3 years, you'll notice your soil is darker and softer. It also holds more water, which is crucial in dry areas. You'll need less irrigation. Onions grown this way often have fewer diseases because soil doesn't splash onto leaves.

One challenge is that soil may be cooler in spring, slowing early growth. In that case, you can clear a small strip for planting. Also, if you have heavy clay, you may need to break it once with a fork. But generally, less disturbance is better. Combine conservation tillage with cover crops and compost for best results. This practice is climate-smart: it stores carbon in the soil, reduces erosion, and makes your farm more resilient to drought. Many African farmers are adopting it successfully.

lessons.title: Biodiversity and Pollinator Habitat
lessons.body:
Biodiversity means having many different plants and animals on your farm. For onions, biodiversity brings pollinators, pest predators, and healthier soil. Onions themselves are pollinated by bees and flies. Without pollinators, seed production drops. But even for bulb onions, having flowers around attracts beneficial insects that eat pests. So set aside at least 5-10% of your land for habitat.

Plant a border of flowers around your onion field. Good choices include sunflowers, marigolds, cosmos, and zinnia. These are easy to grow and provide nectar and pollen. Also plant herbs like basil, coriander, and mintâthey repel some pests. Allow some native grasses and wildflowers to grow. Don't clear all bushes. A hedge of tithonia or moringa can serve as a windbreak and habitat.

Create homes for beneficial insects. Leave some dead wood or rocks for beetles and spiders. Build a small pond or water sourceâfrogs and dragonflies eat mosquitoes and other pests. Avoid all synthetic pesticides, which kill pollinators. If you must spray, do it in the evening when bees are not active. Use only organic sprays like neem or soap.

Diversify your crops. Rotate onions with legumes, cereals, and leafy greens. Intercrop onions with carrots or lettuceâthey confuse pests. Plant fruit trees like mango or papaya around the edges. These provide shade and food. Keep some areas wild. The more diverse your farm, the fewer pest outbreaks you'll have. Studies show that farms with high biodiversity have 30-50% less pest damage. This is nature's free pest control. Plus, you'll enjoy seeing birds, bees, and butterflies. It makes farming more pleasant and sustainable.

quiz.q: How long must you follow organic standards before getting certified?
quiz.explanation: Organic certification requires a 3-year transition period with no prohibited substances.

quiz.q: What is the minimum buffer zone between organic and non-organic fields?
quiz.explanation: A 10-meter buffer prevents chemical drift from neighboring farms.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT allowed in organic onion farming?
quiz.explanation: Synthetic fertilizers are prohibited in organic certification.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of organic certification?
quiz.explanation: Certified organic onions often sell for 20-50% higher prices.

quiz.q: How often does an organic inspector visit?
quiz.explanation: Annual inspections are required to maintain certification.

quiz.q: Which pest is a major problem for onions?
quiz.explanation: Thrips are a common onion pest that suck sap from leaves.

quiz.q: What is the recommended spacing for onions to reduce disease?
quiz.explanation: 10-15 cm spacing allows airflow, reducing fungal diseases.

quiz.q: How many blue sticky traps per acre for thrips?
quiz.explanation: 10 traps per acre help monitor and control thrips.

quiz.q: Which plant can be used as a trap crop for onion maggots?
quiz.explanation: Radishes attract onion maggots away from onions.

quiz.q: What is a good organic spray for downy mildew?
quiz.explanation: Baking soda (1 tbsp per liter) with soap inhibits fungal growth.

quiz.q: Which insect is a natural enemy of aphids?
quiz.explanation: Ladybugs are predators that eat aphids.

quiz.q: How often should you monitor your onion field for pests?
quiz.explanation: Regular monitoring (twice weekly) allows early pest detection.

quiz.q: What is a common cover crop in Africa that fixes nitrogen?
quiz.explanation: Cowpea is a legume that fixes nitrogen from the air.

quiz.q: How much nitrogen can a good cowpea crop add per hectare?
quiz.explanation: Cowpea can add 50-100 kg of nitrogen per hectare.

quiz.q: When should you chop cover crops for green manure?
quiz.explanation: Chopping before flowering maximizes nitrogen and prevents reseeding.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of cover crops?
quiz.explanation: Cover crops protect soil from erosion and improve structure.

quiz.q: What ratio of greens to browns is ideal for compost?
quiz.explanation: One part greens to three parts browns by volume balances carbon and nitrogen.

quiz.q: How often should you turn a compost pile?
quiz.explanation: Turning every 2 weeks adds oxygen and speeds decomposition.

quiz.q: How long should manure be aged before use on onions?
quiz.explanation: Aging for 3 months reduces pathogens and prevents burning plants.

quiz.q: Which manure is richest in nitrogen?
quiz.explanation: Poultry manure has high nitrogen content, so use it sparingly.

quiz.q: What is compost tea?
options: D) A fertilizer from tea leaves
quiz.explanation: Compost tea is made by soaking compost in water to extract beneficial microbes.

quiz.q: What does conservation tillage mean?
quiz.explanation: Conservation tillage minimizes soil disturbance to protect soil life.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of conservation tillage?
quiz.explanation: Conservation tillage increases earthworm populations and soil health.

quiz.q: How deep should you plant onion seeds in conservation tillage?
quiz.explanation: Onion seeds should be planted 2-3 cm deep for proper germination.

quiz.q: What is one challenge of conservation tillage?
quiz.explanation: Soil may be cooler in spring, slowing early onion growth.

quiz.q: How much land should be set aside for biodiversity habitat?
quiz.explanation: Setting aside 5-10% of land for habitat supports pollinators and beneficial insects.

quiz.q: Which flower is good for attracting pollinators?
quiz.explanation: Sunflowers provide nectar and pollen for bees and other pollinators.

quiz.q: When is the best time to spray organic pesticides to protect bees?
quiz.explanation: Spraying in the evening when bees are inactive reduces harm to pollinators.

quiz.q: How much can biodiversity reduce pest damage?
quiz.explanation: High biodiversity can reduce pest damage by 30-50% through natural predation.

quiz.q: What is a good intercrop for onions to confuse pests?
quiz.explanation: Intercropping onions with carrots can confuse pests and reduce damage.
